headline: Citizen Lab found Pegasus spyware on a European lawmaker who investigated its abuse, as Google and the FBI dismantled a 2-million-device proxy botnet and fresh stealers spread across platforms.

emerging_trends.text: Commercial spyware keeps landing on the very officials assigned to rein it in, with Pegasus surfacing twice on former European Parliament member Stelios Kouloglou's phone during his spyware-abuse probe.
Information stealers keep expanding onto macOS, where PamStealer now impersonates the Maccy clipboard app to lift Mac login passwords through PAM prompts.
Phishing-as-a-service platforms industrialize Microsoft 365 credential theft, with ARToken running as an affiliate of the EvilTokens toolkit.

topics.title: Pegasus Infects EU Spyware Investigator
topics.latest_developments: Citizen Lab reported July 3 that former Member of the European Parliament Stelios Kouloglou suffered two Pegasus infections while he sat on the PEGA committee investigating commercial-spyware abuse across the bloc.
topics.summary: NSO Group's Pegasus lets operators read a target's messages, calls, and location. Forensic analysis of Kouloglou's device showed attackers could have gained full access, which one sitting parliamentarian called a direct attack on the rule of law.

sources.title: European Parliament Member Investigating Spyware Was Hacked With Pegasus
Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it
EU Politicians Investigated Pegasus Spyware. Then It Ended Up on One of Their Phones

topics.title: Google and FBI Disrupt NetNut Proxy Botnet
topics.latest_developments: Google and the FBI disrupted NetNut on July 3, severing a residential proxy network built on roughly 2 million compromised Android devices, including smart TVs and streaming boxes.
topics.summary: NetNut rented access to the infected devices so cybercriminals and nation-state actors could route attacks through victims' home connections and mask their identities. The takedown cut off that infrastructure.

sources.title: NetNut proxy network disrupted, 2 million infected devices cut off
Google, FBI Disrupt NetNut Residential Proxy Network Powered by Millions of Devices

topics.title: Bad Epoll and FatFs Flaws Expose Kernels and Devices
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News disclosed July 3 Bad Epoll (CVE-2026-46242), a patched Linux kernel flaw that hands any unprivileged user root across desktops, servers, and Android, sitting in the same stretch of code where Anthropic's Mythos model recently caught a different bug, while runZero disclosed seven still-unpatched flaws in the FatFs filesystem library embedded in millions of devices.
topics.summary: FatFs reads and writes FAT and exFAT media inside security cameras, drones, industrial controllers, and hardware crypto wallets, so its bugs reach far beyond servers. Administrators should apply the Bad Epoll fix now and watch for FatFs firmware updates.

sources.title: New "Bad Epoll" Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Unprivileged Users Gain Root, Hits Android
Unpatched Flaws Disclosed in Filesystem Bundled Into Millions of Embedded Devices

topics.title: ARToken Phishing Service Targets Microsoft 365
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed July 3 ARToken, a phishing-as-a-service platform that operates as an affiliate of the EvilTokens platform and exposes an extensive toolkit built to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts.
topics.summary: ARToken gives lower-skilled criminals ready-made kits to steal Microsoft 365 credentials and session tokens. Defenders should enforce phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and monitor for suspicious OAuth and token activity.

sources.title: ARToken PhaaS exposes EvilTokens' Microsoft 365 phishing toolkit

topics.title: PamStealer Impersonates Maccy on macOS
topics.latest_developments: Jamf Threat Labs flagged July 3 PamStealer, a macOS infostealer shipped as a compiled AppleScript file impersonating the open-source Maccy clipboard manager and abusing PAM checks to capture Mac login passwords.
topics.summary: PamStealer spreads through fake Maccy download sites and siphons sensitive data once installed. Mac users should download software only from trusted sources and treat unexpected AppleScript files as suspect.

sources.title: PamStealer Uses Fake Maccy Sites and PAM Checks to Steal Mac Login Passwords

topics.title: ShinyHunters Steal Medtronic Data on 3.8 Million
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported July 3 that ShinyHunters breached Medtronic's corporate IT systems in April 2026 and stole personal and medical information on 3.8 million people.
topics.summary: Medtronic, the medical-device maker, joins the string of ShinyHunters victims. Affected patients face exposure of personal and health records and should watch for identity-theft and phishing attempts.

sources.title: Medtronic Data Breach Impacts 3.8 Million People

business_politics.title: Weak U.S. Jobs Report Keeps Dollar Soft
business_politics.latest_developments: Thursday's worse-than-expected June nonfarm payrolls kept the dollar weak against major currencies into Friday, with traders watching Japan's Ministry of Finance for signs of surprise intervention.
business_politics.summary: The United States payrolls report released July 2 undershot forecasts, and the dollar has stayed soft against a basket of currencies as markets weigh a cooling labor market and the Federal Reserve's next move.

sources.title: Weak Jobs Data Continue to Weigh on Dollar

business_politics.title: AI Trade Selloff Whipsaws Global Stocks
business_politics.latest_developments: Investors dumped AI-linked shares Thursday, whiplashing tech-heavy indexes across Asia on doubts about the profitability of the AI build-out, and European semiconductor stocks steadied Friday after following the rout.
business_politics.summary: Cracks in the artificial-intelligence trade drove a sharp Thursday selloff in Asian and European chip and tech stocks, and the Wall Street Journal reports private software loans were already deteriorating faster than at any point in five years before the 'SaaS-pocalypse' fears struck.

sources.title: AI Split Asia Into Winners and Losers. The Balance Looks Unsustainable.
Software Loans Hit Rough Patch Even Before AI Fears Triggered SaaS-Pocalypse
European Chip Stocks Rebound After Thursday Selloff

business.title: Mancini's Bread Turns 100
business.latest_developments: Mancini's Bread marked its 100th year in business this week, timing the milestone to the Independence Day holiday.
business.summary: Mancini's Bread, the family bakery known across the Pittsburgh region for its Italian loaves, is celebrating a full century in business.

sources.title: Mancini's Bread celebrating 100 years in business

business.title: Powerboat Racing Returns to Pittsburgh in 2027
business.latest_developments: Organizers announced July 3 that the Formula One Powerboat National Championship will race Pittsburgh's three rivers over the July 4 weekend in 2027, the first time in roughly a decade.
business.summary: The Formula One Powerboat National Championship will bring high-speed racing back to the Allegheny, Monongahela, and Ohio rivers on the July 4, 2027, weekend, returning the event to Pittsburgh after about ten years away.

sources.title: Powerboat racing will return to Pittsburgh waters in 2027
Formula One Powerboat National Championship coming to Pittsburgh in 2027

around_town.title: Parkway East to Close for Bridge Replacement
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT set the start date: it will close the Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and the Edgewood/Swissvale exit at 9 p.m. on July 10 to begin replacing the aging Commercial Street Bridge.
around_town.summary: PennDOT will shut Interstate 376's Parkway East between the Squirrel Hill Tunnel and Exit 77 at Edgewood and Swissvale starting the night of July 10 to replace the deteriorating Commercial Street Bridge near Frick Park.

sources.title: Traffic roundup: Parkway East's Commercial Street Bridge closure approaches

around_town.title: PRT Unveils America250 Light Rail Car
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Regional Transit revealed a specially wrapped light rail vehicle July 3 honoring America250, the national commemoration of the Declaration of Independence.
around_town.summary: Pittsburgh Regional Transit put into service a light rail car wrapped in America250 imagery, marking the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Regional Transit unveils America250-inspired light rail vehicle

around_town.title: Trump Accounts Launch July 4
around_town.latest_developments: The federal Trump Accounts program launches July 4, seeding $1,000 for each qualifying baby born during President Trump's second term into stock-market investments.
around_town.summary: Starting July 4, the White House will deposit $1,000 for each eligible baby born during President Trump's second term, with the money invested in the stock market to grow; families can check whether their child qualifies.

sources.title: Trump Accounts launch tomorrow. Find out if your child qualifies to receive $1,000

events.title: Pittsburgh's July 4 Celebration
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's Fourth of July program, voted the nation's best by USA Today readers, will add a Plain White T's concert, line dancing, and Ferris wheel rides atop the city's largest-ever fireworks show on Saturday.
events.summary: Pittsburgh marks America's 250th birthday Saturday, July 4, with a record fireworks display plus a Plain White T's performance, line dancing, and Ferris wheel rides spanning Downtown, the North Shore, and Mount Washington.

sources.title: Here's what to know about fireworks in Pittsburgh for Fourth of July

events.title: Noah Kahan at PNC Park
events.latest_developments: Folk-pop singer Noah Kahan headlines PNC Park on Friday night, July 3, drawing fans who packed the North Shore ballpark despite the extreme heat.
events.summary: Noah Kahan performs at PNC Park on Pittsburgh's North Shore the evening of Friday, July 3, with crowds arriving early in 90-degree heat.

sources.title: Heat doesn't stop fans from packing PNC Park for Noah Kahan

events.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh BBQ & Bands Fest returns over the holiday weekend, bigger than before with nearly 50 vendors and cover bands, organizers say.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh BBQ & Bands Fest runs the Fourth of July weekend in Monroeville, featuring nearly 50 food vendors and live cover bands.

events.title: Pittsburgh Symphony Budget Jumps to $42 Million
events.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette analysis published July 1 explains why the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's annual budget rose $7 million to $42 million, driven largely by its film-music recording work.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's yearly budget climbed $7 million to $42 million, a jump the Post-Gazette attributes substantially to the orchestra's growing business scoring films.

sources.title: Analysis: Here's why the Pittsburgh Symphony's budget just jumped by $7 million to $42 million

around_teams.title: Steelers Eye Year 2 Defensive Leaps
around_teams.latest_developments: A July 3 Post-Gazette video weighed whether Steelers defenders Derrick Harmon, Jack Sawyer, and others can take second-year jumps in 2026.
around_teams.summary: Post-Gazette Steelers analysts assessed the odds that young defensive linemen Derrick Harmon and Jack Sawyer, among others, make significant second-season leaps for Pittsburgh.

team_usa.title: USMNT Weighs Belgium Without Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: Folarin Balogun spoke publicly for the first time since his red card, calling it an 'emotional rollercoaster' on his 25th birthday, and with his one-match ban confirmed the United States is weighing Ricardo Pepi and Haji Wright to start against Belgium.
team_usa.summary: USMNT striker Folarin Balogun will sit out the World Cup round-of-16 match against Belgium after his sending-off against Bosnia and Herzegovina, leaving Mauricio Pochettino's side to consider Ricardo Pepi and Haji Wright to fill the role.

sources.title: U.S.'s Balogun on ban: 'Emotional rollercoaster'
